title: One-rotation dip changes show no common cubic time arrow in 79 selected TESS CPV stars
abstract: We test whether dip depths in complex periodic variable stars show slow loading followed by sudden loss. We use a bounded signed cubic increment score without selecting large changes or fitting ramps. In 24,225 one-rotation pairs from 565 dip-sector series of 79 stars, the equal-star mean score is -0.0088 (95% star bootstrap interval -0.0542 to +0.0386; whole-star reversal p=0.706). Slow-rise fast-loss injections give -0.3460, reversed injections give +0.3867, and symmetric injections give +0.0336. Sawtooth dips added to real CPV light curves give -0.1138. The weak lag-2 signal does not survive correction for four lags. Signal cuts, extra flare masking, removal of two discovery stars and Gaussian error correction leave the primary result near zero. This supports the earlier event-based evidence against a strong common visible loading and loss cycle. It does not prove reversible dynamics or measure material lifetime. The source depth extraction, fixed phase selection and ideal injection laws limit the test. Original code, input hashes, aggregate results and a figure support reproduction.

display.caption: Signed cubic scores across rotation lags and all planned primary sensitivity checks. Intervals resample whole stars. Negative scores indicate larger depth losses than gains.
